requirement.evidence: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
requirement.note: The "ask for the current figure" advice is added, but the cap and CPI adjustment are stated in the text.

key_value.evidence: The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.
key_value.note: Also matches the actual out-of-pocket cost limit in (b).

status.evidence: (Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67, Sec. 29.   (AB 1170)   Effective January 1, 2026.)
status.note: Presented as current law as of the retrieval date.

citation.evidence: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
citation.note: The cap is in subdivision (b) of § 1950.6; the card cites the section generally.

requirement.evidence: A landlord or their agent shall not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.

status.evidence: (Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67, Sec. 29.   (AB 1170)   Effective January 1, 2026.)

citation.evidence: (c) (1) A landlord or their agent shall not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.

requirement.evidence: (B) An application screening process in which the landlord or their agent returns the entire screening fee to any applicant who is not selected for tenancy, regardless of the reason, within 7 days of selecting an applicant for tenancy or 30 days of when the application was submitted, whichever occurs first.
requirement.note: Both alternatives in (c)(2)(A) and (B) are stated in the text, including the 7-day refund for inadvertent collection.

key_value.evidence: within 7 days of selecting an applicant for tenancy or 30 days of when the application was submitted, whichever occurs first.

status.evidence: (Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67, Sec. 29.   (AB 1170)   Effective January 1, 2026.)

citation.evidence: (2) A landlord or their agent may charge an applicant an application screening fee only if the landlord or their agent, at the time the application screening fee is collected, offers any of the following:

requirement.evidence: The landlord or their agent shall provide, personally, or by mail, the applicant with a receipt for the fee paid by the applicant, which receipt shall itemize the out-of-pocket expenses and time spent by the landlord or their agent to obtain and process the information about the applicant.
requirement.note: The (e) refund duty is also stated, in similar terms.

status.evidence: (Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67, Sec. 29.   (AB 1170)   Effective January 1, 2026.)

citation.evidence: If the landlord or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, the landlord or their agent shall return any amount of the screening fee that is not used for the purposes authorized by this section to the applicant.
citation.note: Subdivisions (d) and (e) match the cited provisions.

requirement.evidence: If an application screening fee has been paid by the applicant, the landlord or their agent shall provide a copy of the consumer credit report to the applicant who is the subject of that report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of the landlord or their agent receiving the report.

key_value.evidence: within seven days of the landlord or their agent receiving the report.

status.evidence: (Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67, Sec. 29.   (AB 1170)   Effective January 1, 2026.)

citation.evidence: (f) If an application screening fee has been paid by the applicant, the landlord or their agent shall provide a copy of the consumer credit report to the applicant who is the subject of that report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of the landlord or their agent receiving the report.
